item.title: Negri Nepote Native Grassland Preserve — Sat Aug 15, 8:30 AM — NJ
item.description:
Led by Chris and Paula Williams, NJ Audubon Associate Naturalists. Join the Williams for a walk through the fields of this grassland preserve to look for resident NJ birds, butterflies, and anything else nature will be showing. Grasshopper Sparrow, Bobolink, and American Kestrel, state threatened species, are found on this site. Bring binoculars if you have them. The trails through the field are easy to walk. This site is one of the first grassland restoration projects NJ Audubon has implemented for Franklin Township Open Space Committee. This program is funded by the Franklin Township Open Space Committee. Cost: Free. Location: Negri Nepote Native Grassland Preserve, 260 Skillmans Lane, Somerset, NJ Registration: Please register with Franklin Township by email: Tara.Kenyon@franklinnj.gov
Source: NJ Audubon

Let's Walk!! **This walk begins at 9:30 AM** Please plan to arrive 5 minutes early. The walk will start promptly.
We'll do the perimeter loop and the lake loop, together they are about 2 miles. The group will do 2 circuits (4 miles) in 90 minutes, but all are welcome to stop after one (or stay longer😁). The path is 100% paved. **Wear comfortable shoes and don't forget your water.**
[Perimeter Loop](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/new-jersey/rahway-river-perimeter-loop?u=i&sh=vgtzxk) [Lake Loop](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/new-jersey/lake-rahway-loop?u=i&sh=vgtzxk)

item.title: 🚶Yanticaw Park Nutley — Fri Sep 11, 9:30 AM
item.description:
Let's Walk!! Meet along Park Drive in Nutley near the Orechio Sports Complex. We'll walk about 3.5 mile through scenic Yanticaw Park, up to Kingsland St. and back. The path is paved and mostly flat.
Please check the event page beforehand in case of any changes. Inclement weather will cancel the walk.
The Yanticaw Park is an Essex County-owned park in Nutley, New Jersey. It is located between Centre Street and Chestnut Street, extending west to Passaic Avenue.
Essex County began purchasing land in 1911 for creation of the park. Wetlands in the park were drained, and a dam was set up to form a lake. The park was completed in 1914. In 1962, the lake, containing a small island was drained and a channel was dug as a continuation of the natural third river from the south.
PLEASE ARRIVE 5 MINUTES **EARLY** SO WE CAN START TO WALK ON TIME

item.title: Tech Talks — Tue Sep 15, 3:30 PM — Montclair Main - Classroom
item.description:
Tech Talks is a free informational series where library staff introduce and explain the technology topics that matter most in today's digital world. Each session takes a closer look at a new or complex topic—whether it's a trending app, an emerging technology, or a platform you've been hearing about but aren't quite sure how to navigate. Through demonstrations and clear, jargon-free explanations, you'll come away with a better understanding of the tech landscape around you. There's no hands-on component, so no devices are needed—just come ready to learn and ask questions.
All are welcome regardless of experience level, and time is reserved at the end of each session for Q&A. Sessions are free and open to the public.
This week's topic is: TBD
